prayerExcerpt.en-US: Let us ask St. Porphyry for a great zeal in keeping this commandment, lest we be led away, as so many are, by a curious and prying mind.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Peçamos a São Porfírio um grande zelo em guardar este mandamento, para que não sejamos desviados, como tantos o são, por uma mente curiosa e indiscreta.

meta.face: A Greek of Thessalonica of about sixty-five, worn lean by desert penance, with a light olive complexion and a DIAMOND-SHAPED face — a NARROW forehead and a NARROW chin, broadest at WIDE, jutting cheekbones; a SHORT, straight nose with a LOW bridge; very LARGE, PROMINENT dark eyes under thin, arched brows; a wide, thin-lipped mouth; a BALD crown with dark-grey hair left long at the back and sides; a long, STRAIGHT, dark beard streaked with grey, narrowing to the breast; the gaze wide and earnest.
meta.basis: No portrait survives. The sixteenth-century fresco at Dionysiou on Mount Athos (Wikipedia lead image, local copy) shows him balding with a long dark beard greying, in a phelonion with crosses; the card keeps those. The relics of the Cross and the church over the temple of Gaza, paved with its marbles, are the book's; his age (bishop at forty-five, died 420) follows Wikipedia on the Vita by Mark the Deacon. The diamond face is our choice.
